input.rationale: IBM's only performance warranty (§5.1(a)) is a reasonable-care-and-skill undertaking with no warranty period, no conformance-to-documentation warranty for the software portions of the Base Components, and no repair/replace or refund remedy; §5.2 makes §5.1 exclusive and §5.4 layers on "AS IS" and no-error-free-operation disclaimers. That fails the fallback checklist (90-day software conformance, 30-day Services warranty, repair/replacement and refund). We therefore insert the missing warranties and remedy inside §5.1 so they are captured by the §5.2 exclusivity carve-in, targeting the fallback level only. IBM's compliance-with-laws covenant (p0063) exists but the preferred-level items (12-month software period, 90-day Services period, malicious code) are not pursued.

mappings.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.

proposal.summary: Add 90-day software conformance warranty, 30-day Services warranty and repair/replace-or-refund remedy to §5.1
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 5.1 gives no conformance warranty, no warranty period and no remedy, so we add a 90-day software-to-documentation warranty, a 30-day Services warranty and a repair/replacement-or-refund remedy. We have placed them in Section 5.1 so they survive the Section 5.2 exclusivity language; this is our fallback position.

ops.text: c. for ninety (90) days following delivery, the software portions of the Base Components will conform in all material respects to their applicable documentation; and d. the Services will conform to the warranty in Subsection 5.1(a) for thirty (30) days following their performance. Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in Subsections 5.1(c) and 5.1(d) is, at IBM's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or Services or a refund of the charges paid for them.
